content.comment_body: How can I set up a measurement to calculate the ratio between two analog signals in [product_name]? In other words, how do I divide one analog signal by another?

Thank you, I was able to figure it out myself. The floating point result was only achievable through a workaround—I had to multiply one value by 100 and display it with an offset for the decimal point. I still don't understand why this process has to be so complicated.
It's important to understand how [product_name] functions. It only works with integer numbers, ranging from -32,768 to 32,767, and does not support floating point values.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are attempting to divide analog signals using [product_name], but face difficulties due to the platform's restriction to integer values and lack of floating point support. Methods for displaying precise ratios rely on workarounds such as scaling and decimal point manipulation, which are not intuitive. Users unfamiliar with these numeric constraints find the process confusing and see a lack of clear documentation to guide them.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect either direct support for floating point calculations, or at least comprehensive documentation with practical guidance and tools to accurately compute and display ratios between analog signals.
